column2: On the Isle of Flame the priests of Asuryan have chanted the warding spells over you since dawn. Now the great doors of the shrine stand open, and the Flame of Asuryan roars cold and white before you. It burned Malekith. It has crowned every true Phoenix King since Aenarion. You step forward.
May Asuryan judge me well.
You walk out of the Flame unburned, the white fire still dancing on your skin. The priests fall to their knees, and outside the shrine the waiting Princes raise the cry: the Phoenix King is crowned!
Asuryan has chosen me.

You enter the Flame with a steady heart, but Asuryan does not favour you. His gaze passes through the warding spells as if they were mist, and the fire sears your flesh. The priests drag you out shrieking, but the god has spoken for all to see: you are not the rightful Phoenix King.
AAAARGH!

You enter the Flame with a steady heart, but Asuryan does not favour you. His gaze passes through the warding spells as if they were mist, and the fire takes you. The priests struggle to pull you out, but your sins must have been great indeed, for they recover nothing but a blackened husk.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has passed through the Flame of Asuryan unburned, proving [From.GetHerHis] right to rule Ulthuan as Phoenix King.
Long live the Phoenix King!
A strange custom, walking into fire.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] tried to pass through the Flame of Asuryan, but the god saw what lay in [From.GetHerHis] heart and burned [From.GetHerHim]. Not since Malekith has the Flame judged so harshly.
[From.GetSheHeCap] cannot wear the crown!
[From.GetSheHeCap] walked into a fire and got burned. What of it?
Your [GetFromRelation] was burned by the holy Flame of Asuryan, and the shame falls on all of [From.GetHerHis] blood. Wherever you go, elves will whisper that the god rejected your line.
But I am not tainted!
The healing spells have slowly mended your body, but the mark of Asuryan remains, burned into your skin and into your soul.
How could this happen to me?

[From.GetTitledFirstName] tried to pass through the Flame of Asuryan, but the god saw what lay in [From.GetHerHis] heart and consumed [From.GetHerHim] entirely. Nothing came out of the shrine but ash.
The gods have unmasked a false king!
Why did [From.GetSheHe] walk into the fire at all?
The Princes of Ulthuan have met in council after the death of [From.GetFirstName] in the Flame. Rather than trust the crown to the blood the god rejected, they have chosen you to rule Ulthuan.
I will rule in the grace of Asuryan.
The Princes of Ulthuan have decided that the crown should pass to [From.GetTitledFirstName] rather than to the blood of the king the Flame consumed. Your birthright has been taken from you.
Pretenders! The crown is mine by right.

Following in the footsteps of the Witch King, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has renounced Asuryan and the gods of Ulthuan. The seeds of a second Sundering have been sown, and every Prince must choose where to stand.
I stand with my king.
I stand with the gods.

The Princes of Ulthuan have argued for centuries over the duty of the Asur. Some say Ulthuan must close its shores and keep itself pure, guarding the Vortex and nothing else. Others say the elves must stand against Chaos wherever it rises, and lead the younger races away from ruin.
We must protect Ulthuan.
We must protect the world.

Your Majesty,

The Princes I speak for must insist that Ulthuan close its shores to the outside world. We are prepared to take up arms should you refuse, and rest assured, we have warriors enough to keep the blood of the Asur safe and pure.

[From.GetTitledName]
Very well. Ulthuan will close its shores.
I will not be commanded!

[Root.GetTitledName],

Your attempt at blackmail has failed. However many fools you have gathered to your cause, I will not give in without a fight. Ulthuan has been shut away for far too long!

[From.GetTitledName]
Then it is war!

[Root.GetTitledName],

I see now what is best for the Asur. I will issue a decree forbidding further dealings with the outside world.

[From.GetTitledName]
Excellent.

[Root.GetTitledName],

Rather than let civil war tear Ulthuan apart, [From.GetTitledName] has agreed to change [From.GetHerHis] policy towards the outside world. Your support in this matter will not be forgotten.

[FromFrom.GetTitledName]
Good.
[From.GetTitledName] has given in to the demands of the Isolationist Princes. Ulthuan closes its shores.
I see.
Defeated in war, you must give the Isolationists what they want. Ulthuan no longer answers the pleas of the outside world, and the good of the Asur comes before all else.
So be it.
Defeated in war, you must give the Interventionists what they want. Ulthuan takes up its old duty as the guardian of the world.
So be it.

Your Majesty,

The Princes I speak for must insist that Ulthuan open its shores and take up its duty to the world. We are prepared to take up arms should you refuse, and rest assured, we have warriors enough to lead Ulthuan out of this shameful idleness.

[From.GetTitledName]
Very well. Ulthuan will open its shores.
I will not be commanded!

[Root.GetTitledName],

Your attempt at blackmail has failed. However many fools you have gathered to your cause, I will not give in without a fight. Ulthuan has no need to meddle in the squabbles of short-lived barbarians!

[From.GetTitledName]
Then it is war!

[Root.GetTitledName],

I see now what is best for the Asur. I will issue a decree opening Ulthuan to the outside world.

[From.GetTitledName]
Excellent.

[Root.GetTitledName],

Rather than let civil war tear Ulthuan apart, [From.GetTitledName] has agreed to change [From.GetHerHis] policy towards the outside world. Your support in this matter will not be forgotten.

[FromFrom.GetTitledName]
Good.
[From.GetTitledName] has given in to the demands of the Interventionist Princes. Ulthuan opens its shores.
I see.
[From.GetTitledFirstName], the legate of your new land across the sea, writes that the colony cannot stand without gold to build walls and quays.
I will pay for it myself.
All the Princes of Ulthuan should share the cost.
We cannot spare it.
As is the custom, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent gold, soldiers and builders from Ulthuan to raise the colony.
Excellent.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has raised a special tax on the Princes to pay for a new colony across the sea under [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName].
I will gladly pay it.
A waste of good gold!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] writes that Ulthuan cannot spare anything for your colony right now.
Have they abandoned us?
[From.GetTitledFirstName], who holds one of Ulthuan's colonies, reports a great victory and has sent a share of the spoils, as is the custom.
I will keep it.
The Princes who supported the colonies should share in it.
One of Ulthuan's colonies has won a great victory, but [From.GetTitledFirstName] has kept every coin of the spoils for [From.GetHerHim]self.
How dare [From.GetSheHe]!
One of Ulthuan's colonies has won a great victory, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] has shared the spoils with every Prince who supported the colonies.
Splendid.
Fair enough, I suppose.
[From.GetTitledFirstName], who holds one of Ulthuan's colonies, has sent a rich tribute to prove [From.GetHerHis] loyalty to the Phoenix Throne.
We graciously accept it for ourselves.
We shall share it with the Princes who support us.
One of Ulthuan's colonies has sent a rich tribute, but [From.GetTitledFirstName] has kept all of it for [From.GetHerHim]self.
How dare [From.GetSheHe]!
One of Ulthuan's colonies has sent a rich tribute, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] has shared it with every Prince who supported the colonies.
Splendid.
Fair enough, I suppose.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] begs the Phoenix Throne to help [From.GetHerHis] colony in its hour of need.
Ulthuan will fight beside our kin!
I will pay for their war myself.
The Princes shall pay to help our kin abroad.
We cannot spare anything right now.
Ulthuan has answered your call, sending gold and soldiers to aid you in your need.
Excellent.
One of Ulthuan's colonies is at war with lesser races, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] has raised a special tax on the Princes to help it.
I will gladly pay it.
A waste of good gold!
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has decided that it is not in the interest of the Asur to help you right now.
Have they abandoned us?
One of Ulthuan's colonies is at war with lesser races, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] has called all of Ulthuan to arms to help it.
Let us sail with them!
Outrageous!
Take heart: [From.GetTitledFirstName] has heard your call, and all of Ulthuan will sail to aid you against your enemies.
Praise Asuryan!
A Prince of Ulthuan has chosen to join your wars.
Excellent.
[From.GetTitledFirstName], who holds one of the Asur colonies abroad, has sent a ship laden with treasure and envoys who beg you to open Ulthuan's shores to the elves across the sea once more.
We accept this gift with an open mind and open harbours.
I thank them for the treasure. The answer is still no.
Your envoys return with a herald of the Phoenix King. [From.GetTitledFirstName] was moved by your plea and has opened Ulthuan's shores again.
At last!
Your envoys return empty-handed. [From.GetTitledFirstName] has kept your treasure, but Ulthuan's shores stay closed.
And what of my ship full of treasure?

War has come to [asur_vale_defender.GetTitledFirstName], the Everqueen herself. [asur_vale_attacker.GetTitledFirstName] means to lay hands on Avelorn and the Gaen Vale, the holiest ground in Ulthuan, where the shrine of Isha stands. Will you sail to defend her?
To war! For the Everqueen!
The gods will protect her.
Ulthuan has closed its shores. You no longer enjoy its protection, but neither do you owe it tribute.
Grim times indeed.

Your Majesty,

I humbly ask on behalf of [From.GetFirstName] that you take [From.GetHerHim] into the Phoenix Court. [From.GetSheHeCap] is young, but a very promising mind, and could only add to the glory of your court.

Awaiting your answer,
[FromFrom.GetTitledName]
I will allow it.
I need no more courtiers.

[Root.GetFirstName],

Your family has persuaded me to give you a chance to show the qualities they claim for you. The Phoenix Court awaits your arrival.

[From.GetTitledName]
An honour!

[Root.GetFirstName],

I regret that the Phoenix Court is already full of young and promising minds. Perhaps I shall have need of you in the future. Not this century, I fear.

[From.GetTitledName]
Damnation.

For some time [From.GetFirstName] has been telling you that if the worst should come, [From.GetSheHe] would want no one but you to inherit [From.GetHerHis] lands and fortune, since [From.GetSheHe] has no children of [From.GetHerHis] own.
I gratefully accept.
We may yet have children. Do not lose hope.

You have talked long with [From.GetFirstName] about what should become of your lands and fortune if the worst should come, with no children to inherit them. At last [From.GetSheHe] has agreed: everything will go to [From.GetHerHim].
Wonderful.
You have talked long with [From.GetFirstName] about what should become of your lands and fortune if the worst should come, with no children to inherit them. But [From.GetSheHe] wants no such burden.
I see.
War or the slow passing of years, it makes no difference: there are fewer elves in [elven_province.GetName] than there were. Such is the fate of the Asur, to dwindle slowly, yet never to yield.
War or the slow passing of years, it makes no difference: [elven_province.GetName] is half empty now. Abandoned villages and silent mansions dot the countryside, their people only a memory.

War or the slow passing of years, it makes no difference: [elven_province.GetName] is all but empty. Its lords struggle to keep up the forms of civilisation, and whole valleys have been given back to the forest and the beasts.
War or the slow passing of years, it makes no difference: [elven_province.GetName] is a ghost of what it was. The great houses still keep their mansions and the lands around them, but little more.
We endure.
On patrol in the hills, [asur_hero.GetTitledFirstName] drove off a band of raiders almost single-handed. The whole court hails [asur_hero.GetHerHim] as a great warrior.
The court shall honour [asur_hero.GetHerHim].
I could have done as well.

[asur_coward.GetTitledFirstName]'s company was ambushed on patrol, and [asur_coward.GetSheHe] fled, leaving [asur_coward.GetHerHis] warriors to die. [asur_coward.GetHerHisCap] name is disgraced, and [asur_coward.GetSheHe] has shamed the whole court.
That was ill done. Let the shame be [asur_coward.GetHerHis] punishment.
Imprison [asur_coward.GetHerHim].
Banish [asur_coward.GetHerHim] for cowardice!

[asur_poet.GetTitledFirstName] has composed a new epic, and it brings tears to the eyes of all who hear it. At the feast table even hardened warriors sit misty-eyed, remembering the glories of your ancient race.
It is like the first light of a winter moon!
I do not care for it.

Manticores, hydras and great lions sometimes come down out of the Annulii Mountains. One has been seen in your lands, and your huntmaster is gathering riders for a great hunt. Will you ride with them, and perhaps win a new trophy for your hall?
Yes, certainly!
No, I think I will sit this one out.

The Phoenix King rules Ulthuan, but the Everqueen is its heart. By ancient custom the two take part in a ritual marriage of a year and a day, and their daughter becomes the next Everqueen. Avelorn has no heir.
Who am I to go against tradition?
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has come to Avelorn to keep the ancient custom: a ritual marriage of a year and a day between the Phoenix King and the Everqueen, so that Avelorn may have an heir.
Who am I to stand against tradition?
You journey to Avelorn and spend many days and nights at the court of the Everqueen. She assures you that her magic will see a child born before long: the next Everqueen.
It is good to be the Phoenix King.
I thought of Ulthuan the whole time, I promise.
Nine months after the Phoenix King's visit, a daughter is born, and all of Avelorn rejoices at the birth of its future Everqueen!
I knew it would be a girl!
Word comes that all of Avelorn and Ulthuan are rejoicing: a new Everqueen has been born, and you are her father.
She will be a great Everqueen one day.
[FromFrom.GetFirstName] thinks you have a gift for magic and has sent you to study with the Loremasters in the White Tower of Hoeth.
A great honour!
The scion of a noble house, [From.GetFirstName], shows a gift for magic and has been sent to study among the Loremasters of the White Tower.
We welcome the new pupil.
Every pupil of the White Tower gives countless hours to study, learning what the Loremasters have gathered in their libraries over thousands of years.
I will do my best.
Your long years of study have paid off at last. You can feel the Winds of Magic answer you, and the Loremasters have named you a Mage of Ulthuan.
For all your efforts, the Winds of Magic do not answer you. The Loremasters have sent you home.
I will use these powers wisely.
I tried my best.
Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has left the White Tower of Hoeth as a Mage of Ulthuan, a great honour for [From.GetHerHim] and for your house.
Splendid.
Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] could not master the Winds of Magic and, after a series of mishaps, has been sent home from Hoeth.
You are a disgrace!
was consumed by the Flame of Asuryan, judged unworthy of the Phoenix Crown
